title: An integrated transcription factor framework for Treg identity and diversity.
authors: Chowdhary, Kaitavjeet; Leon, Juliette; Mathis, Diane; Benoist, Christophe
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
one_liner_zh: 该文结合单细胞染色质可及性、机器学习和遗传变异构建Treg细胞多转录因子整合框架，虽涉及TF调控网络但未聚焦TF-DNA三维互作建模，方法可迁移但深度不足。
abstract: Vertebrate cell identity depends on the combined activity of scores of transcription factors (TF). While TFs have often been studied in isolation, a systematic perspective on their integration has been missing. Focusing on FoxP3+ regulatory T cells (Tregs), key guardians of immune tolerance, we combined single-cell chromatin accessibility, machine learning, and high-density genetic variation, to resolve a validated framework of diverse Treg chromatin programs, each shaped by multi-TF inputs. This framework identified previously unrecognized Treg controllers (Smarcc1) and illuminated the mechanism of action of FoxP3, which amplified a pre-existing Treg identity, diversely activating or repressing distinct programs, dependent on different regulatory partners. Treg subpopulations in the colon relied variably on FoxP3, Helios+ Tregs being completely dependent, but RORgamma+ Tregs largely independent. These differences were rooted in intrinsic biases decoded by the integrated framework. Moving beyond master regulators, this work unravels how overlapping TF activities coalesce into Treg identity and diversity.
abstract_zh: 脊椎动物细胞身份取决于数十种转录因子（transcription factors, TFs）的联合活性。尽管TFs常被孤立研究，但对其整合的系统性视角一直缺失。聚焦于FoxP3+调节性T细胞（regulatory T cells, Tregs）——免疫耐受的关键守护者，我们结合单细胞染色质可及性、机器学习和高密度遗传变异，解析了一个经过验证的多样化Treg染色质程序框架，每个程序均由多TF输入塑造。该框架识别出先前未被认识的Treg调控因子（Smarcc1），并阐明了FoxP3的作用机制，其放大预先存在的Treg身份，根据不同调控伙伴，多样性地激活或抑制特定程序。结肠中的Treg亚群对FoxP3的依赖程度各异，Helios+ Tregs完全依赖，而RORgamma+ Tregs则基本不依赖。这些差异根植于整合框架解码的内在偏向性。超越主调控因子，这项工作揭示了重叠的TF活性如何汇聚成Treg身份与多样性。
